title: Longer warmdown (0.7) + full attention on every layer
description: Two constants: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5->0.7 and WINDOW_PATTERN "SSSL"->"L", so all 10 layers get the full 2048 context instead of 7 of them seeing 1024; HEAD_DIM stays 128, nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.989734 vs the 0.988076 baseline: +0.0017, i.e. a tie on the wrong side, not a win and not a real regression (my pre-registered bar was 0.002). Two variables, and a0 ran pure WARMDOWN 0.7 as the control, so (0.989734 - a0's) is the clean window term. The durable finding is a throughput one and it is large: MFU 46.38%, the highest number recorded in this cell by ~2.5 points, against 41.94% for the baseline. I predicted all-L would cost ~11% of the tokens because it raises FLOPs/token 12.8% (4.29e8 -> 4.84e8). It cost 2.0% (287.3M vs 293.3M, 1096 steps vs 1119). FA3 runs a full causal 2048 window far more efficiently than a 1024 sliding one, so ~85% of the extra FLOPs came out of previously wasted GPU time. Consequence for the group: sliding windows are NOT buying meaningful speed at this size, so the 'S' in the pattern is nearly free to remove -- and, symmetrically, nobody should expect to harvest tokens by shortening windows. Since the quality side came out flat-to-slightly-negative, the honest verdict is that the window axis is a wash in both directions and not worth another slot. Final smoothed train loss 2.774 vs the baseline's 2.752, so the small deficit is optimization-side, not an eval artifact.
